title: Uniform local models and Tor interval for a twisted coefficient dual
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $T$ a scheme. Work with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale site and its derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $a\leq b$ and $m$ be integers, and let $P\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ admit an etale covering on which it is represented by bounded complexes $E^\bullet$ of constant finite projective $A$-modules zero outside $[a,b]$. Here finite projective means a direct summand of a finite free module. Let $L$ be a module sheaf etale locally isomorphic to $A_T$, and put $H=R\mathcal Hom_A(P,L[m])$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then, on a common refinement trivializing $L$, $H$ is represented by $\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(E^\bullet,A)[m]$, with degree-$q$ dual term $\operatorname{Hom}_A(E^{-q},A)$ and differential $d^q(\phi)=(-1)^{q+1}\phi d_E^{-q-1}$ before shifting. Its terms are constant finite projective modules and are zero outside $[-b-m,-a-m]$. In particular $H$ has finite locally constant cohomology, is bounded constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and has Tor amplitude in $[-b-m,-a-m]$: $\mathcal H^i(H\otimes_A^L M)=0$ outside this interval for every degree-zero module sheaf $M$ [def-kun-derived-tensor, def-kun-tor-amplitude].

proof.text: Refine the given etale cover so that P and L on each member U are represented by E^\bullet and A_U. Exact slice restriction is supplied by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identifies the restriction of H with RHom(E^\bullet,A_U[m]). For each i choose a splitting of E^i off A_U^r. Applying internal Hom makes Hom(E^i,-) a functorial retract of Hom(A_U^r,-), which is exact by [lem-sc-finite-free-internal-hom-exact]. Its value on a short exact sequence is a direct summand of the corresponding exact sequence, hence exact. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-exact-term-hom-quasi-iso] to the K-injective resolution A_U[m] -> I(A_U[m]) of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The source E is bounded in [a,b], and its termwise internal Hom functors are exact as just checked. Thus the ordinary Hom complex maps quasi-isomorphically to the complex defining derived internal Hom. The shift compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] gives the required representative Hom_A^\bullet(E^\bullet,A_U)[m].

proof.text: Before shifting, the Hom-complex definition gives in degree q the term Hom_A(E^{-q},A), with differential d^q(phi)=(-1)^{q+1} phi d_E^{-q-1}. If E^i is a retract of A^r, dualizing the two retraction maps makes Hom_A(E^i,A) a retract of A^r, hence finite projective. The cochain shift [m] changes the support from [-b,-a] to [-b-m,-a-m], and the same formula holds after the common trivialization of L.

proof.text: On every member U of the refined cover, the displayed complex has finite constant A-modules as terms, so its kernels and images, and therefore its cohomology, are finite locally constant A-modules. These local descriptions show that each cohomology sheaf of H is lisse on T. The one-piece partition {T} is finite and locally closed, so the definition [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] gives bounded constructibility; the displayed support interval gives boundedness.

source.place: ancestor Proof paragraph 3, local dual-model and constructibility argument

proof.text: Let M be any degree-zero A-module sheaf. On each U, the local dual complex is supported in [-b-m,-a-m]. Its terms are retracts of finite sums of A_U. Tensoring with a term is consequently a functorial retract of a finite direct sum of the identity, so it is exact; the terms are flat. Apply [lem-kun-flat-bounded-tor-amplitude] on the scheme U, with endpoints -b-m <= -a-m (since a <= b). This gives the required vanishing after derived tensor with M|_U. Exact restriction to the slice, from step 1, is its own derived pullback. Applied to this ringed-topos pullback, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies (H tensor^L M)|_U with (H|_U) tensor^L (M|_U), using the derived tensor of [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Exactness also makes restriction commute with cohomology. Each section of the cohomology sheaf outside the interval restricts to zero on the base-changed cover, hence is zero by the sheaf axiom. Therefore the vanishing holds on T for every M, which is precisely [def-kun-tor-amplitude].
